date_note: The release gives only its own publication date (Nov 26) and no access date.
title: New Balance Japan: a maximum of 3.74 million (approximate) customer records affected by unauthorized access to PLAID KARTE
summary: New Balance Japan says unauthorized third-party access to KARTE, a service of its contractor PLAID, affected official online store member data. Its release gives a maximum of 3.74 million (approximate) records of customer number, gender, date of birth and last purchased product, and an approximate 120,000 email addresses stored as hashed strings. Name, phone number, card and password information are not included, it says.
plain: New Balance Japan says a hack of its marketing contractor's service exposed data on a maximum of 3.74 million (approximate) online store members. Names, phone numbers, card data and passwords are not included, it says.
exec: A supplier's tool exposed a maximum of 3.74 million (approximate) records of the company's customers, per New Balance Japan's release.
action: New Balance Japan advises being wary of suspicious emails, SMS or calls impersonating it, not opening unexpected links or attachments, and says it will never ask for card, PIN or password details.

validation.note: New Balance Japan's own release read; Cybersecurity.com (Japan) relays it.
